title: Influence of the Fe<sub>3</sub>O<sub>4</sub>/SiO<sub>2</sub> ratio on the strength and fracture mechanisms of magnetite ore like materials under uniaxial compression
content:
by Tao Yuan, Tianhong Yang, Zhenqi Yang, Qianbai Zhao, Yong Zhao, Jinduo Li, Ke Luo, Yuan Gao

The Fe3O4/SiO2 ratio is an important compositional factor affecting the mechanical behavior of magnetite ore like materials. In this study, uniaxial compression simulations were carried out using particle flow models with different Fe3O4/SiO2 ratios, and the simulated crack evolution and acoustic emission (AE) responses were interpreted together with SEM-EDS observations. The uniaxial compressive strength varies non monotonically with the Fe3O4/SiO2 ratio. As the ratio decreased from 3.00 to 1.00, the peak strength decreased from 131.64 MPa to 81.95 MPa. Further decreases in the ratio to 0.60 and 0.33 increased the peak strength to 146.45 MPa and 151.01 MPa, respectively. At Fe3O4/SiO2 = 1.00, the heterogeneous mineral interfaces appeared highly connected, and cracks preferentially initiated and coalesced along weak SiO2-Fe3O4 and Fe3O4-Al2O3 contacts, producing through going failure paths and the lowest strength. In SiO2 rich specimens, strongly bonded contacts formed a more stable load bearing framework that arrested or deflected cracks and improved strength. Crack number evolution and AE results show that failure was dominated by tensile crack propagation, whereas shear and mixed mode events were mainly associated with late stage coalescence, local sliding, and failure zone formation. SEM-EDS observations provide qualitative microstructural support for this mechanism: Si rich regions tend to impede crack propagation, whereas Si-Fe intergrown regions promote crack linkage. The strength variation is therefore attributed to ratio dependent changes in mineral contact combinations, the continuity of the load bearing framework, and the connectivity of heterogeneous interfaces.
author: Tao Yuan
